title: Propositional proofs: natural deduction, soundness, and completeness
summary: Finite proof trees and truth tables establish the same propositional consequences.
abstract: From ‘both A and B hold’ we can infer A, but from ‘if A then B’ and B we cannot infer A. Natural deduction makes this difference precise by building finite proofs from stated rules and allowing temporary assumptions to be discharged. Every such classical proof preserves truth. Conversely, whenever a conclusion is true under every valuation satisfying a finite set of premises, those premises have a formal derivation of the conclusion. These two results explain why a counterexample valuation rules out a proof and why, for finite premises, having no proof of a contradiction is equivalent to having a satisfying valuation.

based_on.title: Sets, Logic, Computation: An Open Introduction to Metalogic (archived Fall 2025; remix 38828e6, Text 0c1e9e3)
